subject.title: [Feature Request] Infrastructure Expansion: Time to implement Global Mirrors and Load Balancing for OpenClaw

question: Should ClawHub pursue repository-owned multi-region mirrors and automatic failover, or rely on the current hosting providers’ managed edge and availability capabilities?
rationale: Current main has a canonical origin, cacheable reads, artifact-integrity metadata, and sensitive proxy-trust controls but no replica topology; deployment ownership, consistency, security, and operational responsibility cannot be inferred from the empty request.

options.title: Use managed provider edge
options.body: Keep a canonical origin and use provider-managed caching, routing, and availability, adding repository documentation and smoke checks where needed.

options.title: Design owned replicas
options.body: Approve a multi-region architecture covering replication, health routing, invalidation, artifact integrity, moderation enforcement, observability, and rollback.

options.title: Wait for measured need
options.body: Defer implementation until regional latency, availability, or access data establishes concrete targets and priority.

recommendation.title: Use managed provider edge
recommendation.body: Keep a canonical origin and use provider-managed caching, routing, and availability, adding repository documentation and smoke checks where needed.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent main-branch work owns the closest deployment, proxy-routing, cache-delivery, and artifact-serving contracts needed to assess feasibility.
